context: Standing operator confirmation (every found bug: register and fix, never ask); found by the main thread on push CI run 41486371753 (feature/0.8.2 6cd90f9): the [None, 'None'] case fails on all 11 pandas-3.1.0 rows and passes on the pandas-2.2.0 floor row. Reproduced on pandas 3.1.0, numpy 2.5.4, pyarrow: pd.DataFrame({None: [...], 'None': [...]}) has columns [nan, 'None'] (dtype str), and the DataGenerator frame equals that pandas frame in all four cases of the test, so the generator holds the contract and the literal {None: ...} holds only on pandas 2. Severity HIGH: block-list (1), the work branch's push CI is red. Introduced by the cols-rule-refuses-non-string-names RED test 8a623a7.

cause: read_text() without an encoding decodes with the locale codec, cp1252 on Windows, and the workflow files hold UTF-8 bytes
context: Standing operator confirmation (every found bug: register and fix, never ask); found by the main thread on push CI run 41486371753 (feature/0.8.2 6cd90f9): UnicodeDecodeError on all 4 windows-latest rows. Path.read_text() without an encoding decodes with the locale codec (cp1252 on Windows); auto_tag_publish_master.yml, pr_to_development.yml, pr_to_master.yml and test_on_push.yml hold UTF-8 emoji bytes (0x9d, 0x8f) cp1252 cannot decode. The encoding-less read over .github/workflows was introduced by J1.T3 (507bd20) and kept by J1.T5 (b1827a7), which renamed the test and excluded eval.yml; neither commit reached push CI before run 41486371753 (the last green push run, 41316724967 at f440bf6, holds neither). Reproduced on Linux with python -X warn_default_encoding -W error::EncodingWarning. Other text reads with the locale codec: tests/integrations/test_public_api.py:705, evals/run.py:47 and :60, evals/tasks/e1-cold-discovery/tests/check.py:14 (errors='ignore', drops bytes silently). Severity HIGH: block-list (1), the work branch's push CI is red.
expected: .github/workflows/test_on_push.yml runs every Python row on windows-latest; a test reads repo text as UTF-8 on every row
repro: python -X warn_default_encoding -W error::EncodingWarning -m pytest tests/integrations/test_public_api.py::test_no_workflow_but_eval_yml_names_the_evals_folder -> EncodingWarning; on windows-latest: UnicodeDecodeError (CI run 41486371753)
solution: every repo text read passes encoding='utf-8'
symptom: UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d in position 925: character maps to <undefined>
title: The evals-folder workflow test reads workflow files with the locale codec and fails on Windows

cause: The shim's save wrapper read every save destination back with read_artifact, whose csv fallback cannot read a sqlite database, so the read raised inside the agent's script.
context: provenance's docstring promises None when every artifact column equals a column the script generated through rand_engine on a re-run; the shim's save wrapper reads back every save destination with read_artifact, whose csv fallback cannot read a sqlite database, so the read raises inside the agent's script
expected: None: the shim records the sqlite save and leaves the script's outcome unchanged; out.csv passes against its get_df frame
repro: PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<repo>/evals python -c "import _check, sys; print(_check.provenance('work', 'work/s.py', ['out.csv'], python=sys.executable))" where work/s.py saves DataGenerator(spec, seed=1).size(10) with .write.format('sqlite').option('table', 't').save('out.sqlite') and writes the same generator's get_df() to out.csv
solution: The read-back runs only when the writer wrote files (write_format is not sqlite), the same test save itself makes.
symptom: a script that saves a sqlite table and writes out.csv from get_df returns 'provenance: the script exited 1 on re-run: ... UnicodeDecodeError: utf-8 codec can't decode byte 0x89 in position 99' instead of None
title: The provenance re-run crashes the agent's script when it saves to sqlite

cause: The writer passed indent to DataFrame.to_json(lines=True), which spreads a record over several lines, so an accepted option contradicted the one-record-per-line contract.
context: docs/3_WRITING_FILES.md:32 states json is written by pandas with orient records, one record per line; :40 lists indent among the accepted json options, and specs/memory/product/output/writers-and-streaming.md:41 records it. _JsonFile (file_handler.py:211,275) and FileHandler.to_json (:396-397) pass indent to DataFrame.to_json(lines=True), which then pretty-prints each record over several lines. Found by the hotfix review of eval-shim-sqlite-save-crashes-rerun (verdict 2026-11-07T171028Z): the eval shim's save read-back of such a file kills the re-run with JSONDecodeError. master documents the same option (indent=2, pretty-print JSON).
expected: every json file the writer writes holds one record per line (docs/3_WRITING_FILES.md:32), so a JSON-lines reader reads it back
repro: PYTHONPATH=. python -c "from rand_engine import DataGenerator; import pandas as pd; DataGenerator({'a': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 0, 'max': 9}}}, seed=1).size(3).write.format('json').option('indent', 2).save('x.json'); pd.read_json('x.json', lines=True)" raises ValueError: Expected object or value
solution: indent leaves both json accepted-option lists and the docs table; json refuses it like any undocumented option (operator: Drop indent).
symptom: a json save with option('indent', 2) writes records spread over several lines with blank lines between them, and pd.read_json(path, lines=True) raises ValueError: Expected object or value
title: A json save with the documented indent option writes each record over several lines, which no JSON-lines reader can read

cause: read_artifact concatenated a parts directory in name order while rand_engine writers name parts randomly, so two reads of the same seeded parts differed and the order-sensitive value_hash with them
context: read_artifact (evals/_check.py, the directory branch) concatenates a directory's parts sorted by name, and value_hash is order-sensitive. The batch writer names parts part_<uuid>.csv, random on every run, so the agent's run and the re-run concatenate the same seeded parts in different orders. Found by the rc-4 Job 4 review (verdict 2026-11-07T184817Z, INFO) and reproduced on feature/0.8.2 d0488c4: 2 of 6 provenance runs passed.
expected: provenance gives the same answer on every re-run of a seeded script, and a parts directory rand_engine wrote passes (evals/_check.py provenance docstring: None when every artifact column equals a column the script generated through rand_engine on a re-run)
repro: solve.py: DataGenerator({'age': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 0, 'max': 99}}}, seed=1).size(40).write.format('csv').option('numFiles', 2).save('out'); run it once in a work dir, then call _check.provenance(work, work/solve.py, ['out'], python=sys.executable) six times with PYTHONPATH=.:evals: some calls return None, the others the matches-no-frame line
solution: read_artifact sorts a directory's parts by their content as read, so the frame no longer depends on part names
symptom: a seeded save with option('numFiles', 2), graded as its directory, returns provenance: column 'age' of out matches no frame rand_engine generated on some runs and None on others
title: provenance passes or fails at random on a multi-part save directory: the parts' random names set the concatenation order the column hash depends on

context: evals/_check.py provenance copies workdir to a scratch dir without the artifacts, re-runs the script there, and only then reads the delivered artifacts from workdir. A script that writes by an absolute path (or through a link back into workdir) writes into workdir during the re-run, so provenance compares the re-run's output with the re-run's own record. The same read order lets a symlink loop on an artifact path crash the copy (shutil.Error on feature/0.8.2) instead of failing as not delivered. Found by the rc-4 Job 4 review r2 (verdict 2026-11-07T193238Z, MEDIUM bug proposal) and reproduced by the main thread on feature/0.8.2 fa397e2.
expected: provenance reads the delivered artifacts as delivered and never modifies them (evals/_check.py:149 'The re-run happens in a scratch copy of `workdir` without the artifacts, so the originals are only read'; tests/integrations/test_eval_check.py:6-7 'the agent's artifacts are never modified'), so an unseeded script fails layer 2
repro: in an empty work dir W, solve.py is `from rand_engine import DataGenerator; DataGenerator({'age': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 0, 'max': 100}}}).size(10).get_df().to_csv('<W>/out.csv', index=False)` (unseeded, absolute path); run it once, then `PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<repo>/evals python -c "import sys,_check; from pathlib import Path; w=Path('.').resolve(); print(repr(_check.provenance(w, w/'solve.py', ['out.csv'], python=sys.executable)))"` in W prints None (exit 0), and the sha256 of out.csv changes (2278c9e6d663... before, bc84c7847071... after, on feature/0.8.2 fa397e2)
symptom: an unseeded script that writes out.csv by its absolute path passes provenance (None), and the delivered out.csv is replaced by the re-run's output
title: provenance passes an unseeded script that writes its artifact by absolute path: the re-run overwrites the delivered artifact before provenance reads it

cause: REBUILD 7244f63 made unix_timestamps share _date_bounds without the DATE_DIRECTIVES check _dates applies and without a timezone rule, so a %z date_format parses timezone-aware bounds that epoch_seconds, which subtracts a naive epoch, cannot take; the validator accepted a spec neither engine generates (invariant 3)
context: _date_bounds (rand_engine/validators/method_specs.py) parses start and end under date_format and only compares them, so a %z format yields timezone-aware bounds that validate. Both engines convert bounds with epoch_seconds (rand_engine/core/_np_core.py:23), which subtracts a naive epoch, so every aware bound raises TypeError at generation: SparkGenerator.get_df raises it raw, and DataGenerator refuses it only through its construction-time probe. Found by the rc-4 Job 7 review (verdict 2026-11-07T232139Z, MEDIUM bug proposal) and reproduced by the main thread on feature/0.8.2 8d1914e.
expected: a spec that validates generates (specs/constitution.md:34, invariant 3: 'a validator accepts only methods and parameters the target engine runs'), so a timezone-aware bound is refused with a message naming the column
repro: with Java 17 and PYTHONPATH=<repo>: python -c "from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, functions as F; from rand_engine import SparkGenerator; from rand_engine.validators.common_validator import CommonValidator; spec = {'d': {'method': 'unix_timestamps', 'kwargs': {'start': '2020-01-01 +0000', 'end': '2021-01-01 +0000', 'date_format': '%Y-%m-%d %z'}}}; print(CommonValidator.validate_spark_spec(spec)); spark = SparkSession.builder.master('local[1]').getOrCreate(); SparkGenerator(spark, F, spec).size(3).get_df().collect()" prints [] and then raises TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes (feature/0.8.2 8d1914e)
solution: _date_bounds refuses a bound whose parse carries a tzinfo as it parses it, before any comparison: one rule for every caller, so the mixed aware/naive pair is refused too; tests/test_1_common_validator.py test_timezone_aware_date_bounds_are_refused_by_both_engines pins the full message on both validators
symptom: a unix_timestamps column with start '2020-01-01 +0000', end '2021-01-01 +0000' and date_format '%Y-%m-%d %z' passes CommonValidator.validate_spark_spec ([]), then SparkGenerator(spark, F, spec).size(3).get_df() raises TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
title: unix_timestamps validates timezone-aware start and end bounds that neither engine can generate: SparkGenerator.get_df raises TypeError
